passage:
A river city installed floating barriers to catch plastic before it reached the sea. The barriers guided trash toward a collection point where workers removed it.
At first, people praised the project. The river looked cleaner. But environmental groups reminded the city that catching trash downstream was not enough. The trash still came from homes, shops, and streets.
The city then began education programs and added trash bins near busy areas.
The floating trap was useful, but it was like catching leaves after they fell. To solve the problem, people also had to look at the tree.
Cleaning pollution is good. Preventing it is better.
